title: Edges and pulse counter
summary: Use a CTU counter to count three discrete pulses and reset the count.
scope: Passing means your program behaved correctly in the simulator on this computer. It says nothing about a real machine, its timing or its safety, and it does not show how a real sensor bounces or what a real input does with a pulse shorter than a scan.
objectives: Count the rising edges of an input with a CTU instance called on every scan, so that a long pulse counts once.
Turn an output on when the count reaches its preset, and clear the count with a reset input.

stages.title: Objective
stages.body: In src/EdgeCounter.st the inputs PulseInput and Reset and the output CountReached are declared, and the program writes FALSE to CountReached. Make CountReached turn ON at the third rising edge of PulseInput and stay ON until Reset clears the count. You declare the counter yourself.
stages.checkpoint: You can say why a counter counts rising edges and not the scans in which its input is TRUE, and what its preset PV and its reset R do.

stages.title: Predict
stages.body: The scenario gives PulseInput three pulses, rising at {{t:10}}, {{t:30}} and {{t:50}} ms, and presses Reset at {{t:70}} ms. Predict CountReached at {{t:0}}, {{t:10}}, {{t:30}}, {{t:50}} and {{t:70}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: CountReached stays OFF at {{v:EdgeCounter.CountReached=false@0|0}}, {{v:EdgeCounter.CountReached=false@10|10}}, and {{v:EdgeCounter.CountReached=false@30|30}} ms; turns ON at {{v:EdgeCounter.CountReached=true@50|50}} after the third edge; returns OFF at {{v:EdgeCounter.CountReached=false@70|70}} with Reset.

stages.title: Edit
stages.body: Correct the starting program, save it, then press {{ui:learn.check}}. The starter never counts: it writes FALSE to CountReached, so CountReached stays OFF after the third pulse. Change it so that CountReached turns ON at the third rising edge of PulseInput and Reset turns it OFF again. Write the declaration and the statements yourself.
stages.checkpoint: {{ui:learn.check}} reports the scenario of this lesson as passed.

stages.title: Run
stages.body: Press {{ui:learn.check}}. ZPLC runs your saved program against the scenario of this lesson and lists every assertion that failed.
stages.checkpoint: The scenario is named EdgeCounter and contains {{assertions}} assertions.

stages.title: Observe
stages.body: Follow PulseInput and CountReached in the trace: nothing changes on the first two pulses, CountReached rises with the third at {{t:50}} ms, and it falls when Reset rises at {{t:70}} ms.
stages.checkpoint: CountReached rises once, at the third rising edge, and falls once, with Reset.

stages.title: Reflect
stages.body: Imagine that the third pulse stays TRUE until the end of the scenario. Does CountReached change? Then imagine the counter called only inside IF PulseInput THEN ... END_IF: what does it count?
stages.checkpoint: A long pulse has one rising edge, so it counts once and CountReached is the same. Inside the IF the counter is called only while PulseInput is TRUE, so it never sees PulseInput FALSE, never sees a rising edge after the first one and stops counting.

hints.text: A CTU already counts only rising edges of CU, so a long pulse still counts once; you do not need to detect the edge yourself.
Declare Count : CTU, call it every scan as Count(CU := PulseInput, R := Reset, PV := 3) and copy Count.Q to CountReached.

faultCases: The starter never counts: it writes FALSE to CountReached, so CountReached stays OFF after the third pulse.
